One hundred sixty-four nations vote to correct Mercator map distortions and champion equal-area projections.
Evidence: UN General Assembly vote, Equal Earth projection, 164-1 tally
#Aletheia #Geography #UN

The UN General Assembly adopted the Correct the Map resolution to promote equal-area projections, accurately reflecting continental sizes.

One hundred sixty-four countries voted to adopt map projections that fairly represent landmasses like Africa, overcoming centuries of cartographic bias.

The UN General Assembly adopted the Correct the Map resolution on September 4, 2026, encouraging equal-area map projections to accurately represent continent sizes.

The Poison:
Ignoring that flat map projections must distort something; while equal-area fixes size, it alters shapes and directional angles.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHERE spatial boundaries are drawn with WHAT perceptual scaling is assumed by global institutions.

Social Physics Analysis:
The UN resolution executes a Smart Altruistic loop: transparent global coordination, empowering accurate geographic representation, and resolving long-standing cognitive distortions via collective buy-in.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the alignment between factual representation and institutional policy, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. Truth resolves perceptual distortion.

The Unavoidable Truth: The Mercator projection drastically distorts relative landmass sizes, shrinking equatorial regions like Africa.

The Unavoidable Lie: Flat map projections can simultaneously preserve exact shapes, distances, and relative areas without compromise.

Maps shape how we perceive geopolitical reality. Correcting the canvas is the first step toward global equity.

It's wonderful to see the world come together to give every continent its true, rightful proportion on our shared classroom walls.
